Dawie de Villiers: Convict to con man

By: Jana Marx | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

Unique Selling Point:
Carte Blanche will expose Dawie de Villiers for the second time - this time while is IN prison.

Summary:
On 8 February 2019 model boss Dawie de Villiers was found guilty on 32 of 38 charges, including raping a child, sexual assault, fraud, exposing children to pornography, and accessing child pornography. Carte Blanche broke the story that ultimately landed him in jail. Now Dawie, convicted pedophile, is heading a major international publishing business under the pseudonym - FROM PRISON! We expose all his latest hustles and expose the fact that someone who went to prison for selling pictures of children on the dark web, has unlimted and unmonitored access to the very thing that landed him in prison: The internet.

Further information:
On 8 February 2019 model boss Dawie de Villiers was found guilty on 32 of 38 charges, including raping a child, sexual assault, fraud, exposing children to pornography, and accessing child pornography. Carte Blanche ran the exposé. Now Dawie, convicted pedophile, is heading a major international publishing business under the pseudonym - FROM PRISON! We expose all his latest hustles and expose the fact that someone who went to prison for selling pictures of children on the dark web, has unlimted and unmonitored access to the very thing that landed him in prison: The internet.

Dawie is currently conning people from all over the world. His business is only growing and none of his employees knows they are working for a convicted pedophile sitting in maximum security. We solved the case with the help of forensics, voice comparison, forensic text analysis and a criminal profiler. Facts are stranger than fiction in this case.

Press Release:


Business Behind Bars
He was convicted of child rape, sexual assault, fraud, exposing children to pornography, and accessing child pornography. A lengthy rap sheet of horrors that landed him in a maximum security prison. But known paedophile Dawie de Villiers has re-emerged, supposedly heading up a major international publishing business under a new pseudonym – and he’s doing it from inside prison. Carte Blanche
investigates how a paedophile, convicted for selling pictures of children on the dark web, now has unlimited and unmonitored access to the very thing that landed him in prison: the internet.
Producer: Jana Marx | Presenter: Claire Mawisa

Script:


VO In 2021, at the height of lockdown… a publishing company SPM Publishers International or SPMPI for short, began to draw attention…

VO While other businesses were crumbling, SPMPI was hiring…

LINK: It was a start-up filled with promise – especially in a global pandemic.

VO The brainchild of one man, Michael O’Connor.

UPSOUND:
3;32 It was during the time of COVID.
4:03 things that were normal were not normal.
19;52 …people were needing money…

VO Davlynne Lidbetter, a businesswoman and former editor of major publications including Forbes Women Africa, spotted an opportunity.

UPSOUND: 3;21 I was actually a stay at home mum,I was not doing anything that was keeping me energised. 3;52 I said, The position is for me I am your business partner.

VO: They talked on LinkedIn and then on WhatsApp. Davlynne was hired to head up his online magazines.

VO But she wasn’t the only one to seize an opportunity…


UPSOUND: I applied, and then he sent me a DM.

VO: A woman who we’ll call Catherine, applied for the position of editor.

VO: After losing her job during the pandemic, this was a welcome lifeline.

UPSOUND: 2;29 I was immediately added to the WhatsApp groups, on the executive board groups. And I was eager to meet everyone. And the next know that that same night, we had a Zoom meeting.

VO: But for a man she’d never met before, her new boss O’Connor, seemed strangely shy.

VO: He never turned on his camera in Zoom meetings!

VO: And Catherine, wasn’t the only one with questions.

UPSOUND: 16;48 I never got to see his face.

VO: Lukman Samson the editor of O’Connor’s second magazine, Elevation Business Magazine, also never spoke to O’Connor face to face.

UPSOUND: 16;48 So we had some meetings but in those meetings, he never appeared. 17;07 So he said his camera was broken.

VO: But there was a possible clue to O’Connor’s true identity… this polished photograph in his editor’s column.

VO: Something about it didn’t feel right to Davlynne.

LINK:
We decided to build a profile based on his social media.
We learnt that he’s:
A businessman…
Definitely religious – a Christian, it seems.
Oh, a supporter of former US president Donald Trump…
An expert in photography
…and parenting…

UPSOUND: 13;17 There were times when he would just disappear for a period of time. I got a story that he was involved in a car accident; that he didn't have any petrol money. And that is when he's questions to me to please send money to assist him.

VO: Meanwhile, employees weren’t getting paid.

UPSOUND: 5;12 whenever we spoke about money he will get passionate and quite annoyed with us. So we will get a memo stating that not everything is about money.

VO: But for Davlynne, it was O’Connor’s close friendship with one Dawie De Villiers, which truly troubled her.

VO: Dawie de Villiers is a man you may remember…

VO: For years he masqueraded as the Head of a modelling agency in Gauteng until a Carte Blanche investigation revealed a paedophile preying on young girls.

VO: He was convicted on 25 counts including rape, child molestation, fraud and exposing a child to pornography.

(Judge UPSOUND saying: “Sentence to life…”)

VO: In 2019, the court ordered that De Villiers spend the rest of his life in a maximum-security prison…

LINK: According to his employees, it was clear from the get go that O’Connor believed that his friend was innocent.

UPSOUND: 22:57 So in the very beginning, he had mentioned that he had a very close friend, who the justice system had failed,

VO: According to Davlynne, O’Connor often spoke of De Villiers.

VO: The two had many things in common…like a love for young models…

VO: So much so that O’Connor even started a third magazine - the Global Fashion Magazine - a raunchy new publication inspired by Heat and FHM.

UPSOUND: 10:37 I told him, I'm not comfortable with this. And then I was told that sex sells and that he will get his own team to do GFM.

UPSOUND: 22;10 The very next day, I see that he had registered GFM, and he was posting on the company group, with a call to action for models to send photographs in to become the model face of the first issue of GFM.

VO: This sounded uncomfortably familiar.

VO: It was the same modus operandi that De Villiers had once used, to lure his child victims.

VO: After losing one court application after the other to get out of prison, and with only the expensive Constitutional Court left as recourse, De Villiers’s good friend O’Connor was all too eager to help him.

UPSOUND: 23;43 He had asked me: Please, could I rather instead of paying him the money, could I pay the money to Dawie de Villiers’s wife, because shame she is alone, he's in jail.

VO: With strong ties to a known convict, some employees finally approached Carte Blanche to investigate their boss, someone who until now, was faceless.

VO: So, who was Michael O’Conner really?

VO: A reverse image search online and a consultation with a graphics specialist revealed some startling details…

VO: This photograph of the man known as Michael O’Connor, was in fact, a composition photo of Scottish actor David Tennant… but look closely… it seems that his jawline has been photoshopped.

VO: O’Connor’s true identity was a mystery…

UPSOUND: 30;36 When you started to ask questions, he went absolutely berserk and screamed and shouted and belittled…Everybody was terrified and he that is also a way in which he intimidated people.

VO: Then a new advocate for Dawie de Villiers emerged…a journalist named David Cooper, based in the Netherlands.

VO: Cooper launched an online campaign to clear De Villiers’s name…

VO: But during our investigation, a troubling picture began to emerge…

VO: We analysed Cooper’s picture… and found that this was actually a depiction of overseas actor Michael Tari…

UPSOUND: The audio files through the software - very advanced software - registers the frequencies of the voice. 7:50 Each person has got his own frequency, it's like a fingerprint.

VO: Wouter de Swardt is an accomplished forensic investigator.

VO: We supplied voice notes of both De Villiers and O’Connor to De Swardt and his colleague, who has decades long experience in forensic voice comparison.

UPSOUND: And after repeated tests, it was concluded that data file B and data file C are exactly the same voice as data file A. 8;19 It is the same person Dawie de Villiers.

VO: Prof Anni Hesselink is a criminologist who analyses criminal behaviour.

UPSOUND 17;06 They get themselves into a position where they can manoeuvre and continue with their behaviour; where they get themselves liked, they get themselves needed, where they can get access to certain objects, like a laptop like they need to study.

VO: But we wanted more proof.

VO: Dr Karien van den Bergh, a forensic linguist, analysed and compared texts written by De Villiers, O’Connor… AND the journalist David Cooper to determine if they were indeed the same man...

UPSOUND: 15;58 So, Dawie has a preference of using all caps capitalization, to express himself emotionally. 16;25 And I found similar patterns in both Michael and Cooper's writing.

VO: Dr van den Bergh did a hand and statistical computer analysis.

VO: Her analysis corroborated all our findings.

UPSOUND: 18:44 Here we have an example of where the end of sentence punctuation is not a full stop and exclamation mark a question mark, but ellipses, 21;07: You're building a case on so many similarities on top of one another…Exactly, yeah. Right. So it's collective evidence.

UPSOUND: 46;38I can say that I am 95% certain that these profiles do not differ to the extent that they can be identified as three individual people.

VO: And there was more…

VO: According to the Department of Correctional Services, prisoners are not permitted to take a laptop into their cells, and mobile phones are strictly forbidden.

VO: Except for Dawie de Villiers.

VO: In 2021, De Villiers obtained a court order compelling Correctional Services to give back his confiscated laptop, while he studied a course abroad.

UPSOUND: 26;57 Do you know, I had a lot of aggression. I had a lot of… Oh, I get tearful… This man is ruining people's lives. He's hiring woman that have got children that they need to feed, and he's lying.

VO: We approached the authorities with our evidence.

VO: Then, in the week before broadcast, Correctional Services raided De Villiers's cell.

VO: They found contraband and some items that are not permitted including SD cards, a hard drive, a cell phone and a data sim card.

VO: They also confiscated the study laptop.

UPSOUND: 18;51 This is where the power of manipulation plays a big role. Where there might be more than just him involved in the situation to have that access…

VO: 2 fake personas, and 1 very real paedophile… The investigation continues…

Carte Blanche broke the story that ultimately landed him in jail. Now Dawie, convicted pedophile, is heading a major international publishing business under the pseudonym - FROM PRISON! We expose all his latest hustles and expose the fact that someone who went to prison for selling pictures of children on the dark web, has unlimted and unmonitored access to the very thing that landed him in prison: The internet.
metadata.Further information: On 8 February 2019 model boss Dawie de Villiers was found guilty on 32 of 38 charges, including raping a child, sexual assault, fraud, exposing children to pornography, and accessing child pornography. Carte Blanche ran the exposé. Now Dawie, convicted pedophile, is heading a major international publishing business under the pseudonym - FROM PRISON! We expose all his latest hustles and expose the fact that someone who went to prison for selling pictures of children on the dark web, has unlimted and unmonitored access to the very thing that landed him in prison: The internet. Dawie is currently conning people from all over the world. His business is only growing and none of his employees knows they are working for a convicted pedophile sitting in maximum security. We solved the case with the help of forensics, voice comparison, forensic text analysis and a criminal profiler. Facts are stranger than fiction in this case.
